rounds.text: RBZ Jewellers demonstrates exceptional operational execution, generating 54% TTM profit growth [E19] and a 43% 5-year sales growth CAGR [E14] while maintaining superior return metrics with a 22.0% ROCE [E12] and 20.1% ROE [E13] that substantially outperform sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Despite these strong fundamentals, the market misprices the company at a low P/E of 11.4x [E1] and EV/EBITDA of 7.91x [E11], representing a sharp discount to the sector benchmark P/E of 27.73x [E6] and sector EV/EBITDA of 14.85x [E11]. This disconnect is reinforced by a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 580 per share against a price of Rs 161 [E39], providing a 72.2% margin of safety [E40], while a reverse DCF indicates the market implies just 0.3% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E41]. Forward growth is firmly backed by management targeting INR 800 crores to INR 900 crores in revenue for FY27 [E71], expanding its retail network into Surat, Rajkot, and Ahmedabad [E76, E77], and leveraging existing capacity utilization of only 50% to 55% [E83]. The overall setup is further supported by macro sector tailwinds [E64, E66], a high relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E45], and a rules-based screen score of 89 out of 100 [E56]. Conceded: cash generation remains constrained with operating cash flow at Rs -7 Cr [E29] and free cash flow at Rs -40 Cr [E30], while borrowings increased to Rs 170 Cr [E33] alongside institutional outflows [E36, E37, E38]. However, this cash drain reflects an aggressive capex build-up, highlighted by a 733.3% expansion in CWIP [E34] aimed at capturing steady consumer demand in occasion wear [E73, E75].

Conceded: RBZ Jewellers has delivered strong historical performance, including a 5-year compounded sales growth of 43% [E14], a 5-year compounded profit growth of 42% [E17], and robust returns with an ROE of 20.1% [E13] and ROCE of 22.0% [E12]. However, this profitability is not translating into actual liquidity, as evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -7 Cr [E29], a negative cash conversion of -0.13x [E28], and a deeply negative free cash flow of Rs -40 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30]. To sustain itself, the company has increased its leverage, with borrowings rising to Rs 170 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 91 Cr a year earlier [E33]. This financial strain is compounded by operational headwinds, including a 12% year-on-year decline in quarterly wholesale revenue to INR 70 crores [E86], a contraction in quarterly operating margin to 15% from 17% in the year-ago quarter [E25], and decelerating earnings growth [E61]. Unsurprisingly, institutional investors are exiting, with foreign holdings plunging from 4.33% to 0.03% [E36] and domestic holdings dropping from 3.03% to 0.01% [E37], leading to a negative institutional money flow [E38] and overall institutional outflow [E62]. Finally, shareholders face high risk without any yield, as the stock has an annualised volatility of 58.4% [E48], a historical drawdown of -57.4% [E47], and pays a 0.00% dividend yield despite reporting repeated profits [E4], [E55].

Conceded: operating cash flow turned to Rs -7 Cr [E29], free cash flow reached Rs -40 Cr [E30] with cash conversion at -0.13x [E28], and borrowings rose to Rs 170 Cr [E33]; however, this cash burn reflects active capital reinvestment, as CWIP surged 733.3% [E34], capacity utilization sits at 50% to 55% [E83], and bank line utilization of INR 110 Cr to INR 115 Cr remains comfortably within sanctioned limits of INR 255 Cr [E85]. While quarterly wholesale revenue fell 12% [E86] and quarterly operating margin compressed to 15% [E25], overall operational momentum remains strong with trailing twelve-month profit growth accelerating to 54% [E19], full-year EBITDA rising 43% with margin expanding 233 basis points to 14.44% [E79], and management projecting FY27 revenue to reach INR 800 Cr to INR 900 Cr [E71]. This revenue trajectory is supported by physical retail store expansions into Surat, Rajkot, and Ahmedabad targeted for Q2 FY27 [E76], [E77], sustained occasion-wear demand [E73], and aggressive design launches averaging up to 12 new designs per day [E84]. Conceded: foreign and domestic institutional holdings have dropped [E36], [E37], [E62], dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], [E55], and historical volatility is 58.4% [E48] with a -57.4% maximum drawdown [E47]; yet promoter ownership remains rock-solid at 75.00% [E35]. Crucially, the market has over-penalized these temporary friction points, leaving the stock trading at an attractive P/E of 11.4x [E1] versus the sector's 27.73x [E6], an EV/EBITDA of 7.91x [E11] against the sector's 14.85x [E11], a DCF margin of safety of 72.2% [E40], and a reverse DCF that prices in a negligible earnings growth requirement of just 0.3% [E41].

While the bull views the capital build-up as positive [E34], the reality is that the company's aggressive expansion is heavily debt-funded, with borrowings surging to Rs 170 Cr from Rs 91 Cr [E33] to cover a negative operating cash flow of Rs -7 Cr [E29] and negative free cash flow of Rs -40 Cr [E30], all while existing capacity utilization remains low at 50% or 55% [E83]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth is 54% [E19] and full-year EBITDA margins expanded to 14.44% [E79], but quarterly operating margins have already compressed by 2 percentage points to 15% [E25], the yearly operating-margin trend is inconsistent [E26], and wholesale revenue declined by 12% [E86] as overall earnings growth is decelerating [E61]. Conceded: promoter holding is stable at 75.00% [E35], yet the near-total exit of foreign institutions to 0.03% [E36] and domestic institutions to 0.01% [E37] represents a massive institutional outflow [E62] and negative money flow [E38] that signals deep professional skepticism. Conceded: the P/E of 11.4x [E1] and EV/EBITDA of 7.91x [E11] are below sector benchmarks [E6], [E11], and the DCF suggests a margin of safety [E40], [E41]. However, the price-to-book ratio of 2.26x is actually higher than the sector benchmark of 2.12x [E7], and public shareholders receive a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], [E55] while enduring an annualized volatility of 58.4% [E48] and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -57.4% [E47].

Conceded: operating cash flow was Rs -7 Cr [E29] and free cash flow stood at Rs -40 Cr [E30], as borrowings expanded to Rs 170 Cr [E33]. However, this spending reflects a productive capex build-up given the 733.3% surge in CWIP [E34] to fund retail expansion into Surat and Rajkot by Q2 FY27 [E77], while existing 50% to 55% capacity utilization [E83] offers immediate room to scale toward management's target of INR 800 to 900 Cr revenue in FY27 [E71] supported by unutilized bank limits within a total INR 255 Cr sanction [E85]. Despite a 12% decline in quarterly wholesale revenue [E86] and a slight dip in quarterly operating margin to 15% [E25], the broader business trajectory remains dominant, evidenced by TTM profit growth of 54% [E19], full-year EBITDA margin expansion of 233 basis points to 14.44% [E79], and sector-leading ROE of 18.28% [E9] and ROCE of 18.74% [E10]. Conceded: institutional selling reduced foreign and domestic holdings to 0.03% [E36] and 0.01% [E37] respectively, but promoter alignment remains at the maximum limit of 75.00% [E35] while daily design launches of up to 12 per day [E84] capture steady occasion wear demand [E73], [E75]. Finally, while the price-to-book ratio of 2.26x sits slightly above the sector benchmark of 2.12x [E7] alongside a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], [E55], the business trades at a deeply discounted P/E of 11.4x [E1] versus sector's 27.73x [E6] and EV/EBITDA of 7.91x [E11], yielding a 72.2% margin of safety [E40] where current pricing assumes a mere 0.3% earnings growth [E41].

While the bull defends the capital expenditure build-up [E34], [E77], the company's negative operating cash flow of Rs -7 Cr [E29] and negative free cash flow of Rs -40 Cr [E30] are driven by a highly inefficient cash conversion rate of -0.13x [E28], forcing borrowings to balloon to Rs 170 Cr [E33] despite existing capacity utilization sitting at a low 50% to 55% [E83]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth is 54% [E19], full-year EBITDA margins expanded to 14.44% [E79], and ROE and ROCE outperform sector benchmarks [E9], [E10]. However, the 12% decline in quarterly wholesale revenue [E86], the drop in quarterly operating margin to 15% from 17% in the year-ago quarter [E25], and an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend [E26] all confirm that earnings growth is decelerating [E61]. Conceded: promoters maintain a 75.00% stake [E35] and the company continues to launch new designs [E84] to capture occasion wear demand [E73], [E75]. Yet, this does not offset the massive risk signaled by the near-total exit of institutional investors, with foreign holdings dropping to 0.03% [E36] and domestic holdings to 0.01% [E37], resulting in a clear negative institutional money flow [E38], [E62]. Conceded: the stock trades at a P/E of 11.4x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 7.91x [E11] with a high DCF margin of safety [E40], [E41]. However, this depressed valuation is justified because the company refuses to pay dividends despite repeated profits [E4], [E55], while exposing investors to an annualized volatility of 58.4% [E48] and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -57.4% [E47].
